newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP CHAIRMAN SAYS BOARD BACKS PRESCOTT.
newsitem.headline: BHP CHAIRMAN SAYS BOARD BACKS PRESCOTT.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd chairman Jerry Ellis said in a letter to shareholders that managing director John Prescott had the full support of board.
"The board is unanimous in its support of the managing director and in the strategies he is implementing," Ellis said in the letter.
He said a lot of media attention had been focused on BHP last week after the resignation of three of its top executives and he wished to put these announcements in perspective.
On Friday, BHP said petroleum division chief John O'Connor had resigned due to irreconcilable differences with the board of the giant minerals, petroleum and steel company.

The resignation compounded market concern after the surprise announcements over the previous two days that minerals division chief, Dick Carter and iron ore head, Geoff Wedlock, would take early retirement.
Ellis said the board had embarked on a strategy to achieve higher levels of earnings and lift return on equity last May.
This strategy involved completing a review of the asset base, new projects and projects under construction to lift performance and maximise benefits from new projects.
Minerals chief Carter's resignation coincided with a statement about cost overruns at BHP's Pilbara hot briquetted iron (HBI) project in Western Australia.
At a media briefing on Friday, Prescott linked Carter's exit with the management of the Pilbara HBI project and said the company strived to ensure its projects were under control.

"The review and the strong emphasis on accountability has led to some departures in the management ranks. However, long term planning for succession and training means that BHP has excellent candidates to assume these positions," Ellis said.
At 10.15 a.m (0015 GMT) BHP shares were 19 cents higher at A$17.20, giving it a market capitalisation of A$34.22 billion.
